8.title: Read the chromosome model without assigning blame
8.prompt: Explain why XX/XY probabilities do not justify blaming a parent.
solution: The textbook human model uses X-bearing eggs and X- or Y-bearing sperm: fertilisation can yield XX or XY with equal expected probability.
A typical egg contributes X; the sperm’s X or Y contribution determines the textbook XX/XY combination. Each fertilisation is independent; a family need not have equal numbers.
This describes typical chromosomal sex determination, not every variation in sex development or gender identity. Neither parent chooses the outcome, and blaming a mother is scientifically unfounded.
